question: Should the established catalog-feed URLs remain backward-compatible while signed DSSE and sharded-root consumers are rolled out, or may this deployment intentionally replace the current wire format and fail closed without signing configuration?
rationale: The code can mechanically preserve or replace the old endpoint, but choosing the permanent public protocol and signing-key rollout policy is a maintainer-owned compatibility and trust-boundary decision.

options.title: Stage a versioned signed rollout
options.body: Preserve the legacy atomic response at the existing URL and expose the signed/sharded protocol through a versioned or explicitly negotiated path until compatible consumers are released and proven.

options.title: Accept the breaking activation
options.body: Provision signing configuration and coordinate a consumer release, then intentionally replace the existing endpoint representation with the signed protocol.

options.title: Pause this slice
options.body: Hold the public-route switch until the predecessor protocol work and a signing-key rollout plan have maintainer approval.

recommendation.title: Stage a versioned signed rollout
recommendation.body: Preserve the legacy atomic response at the existing URL and expose the signed/sharded protocol through a versioned or explicitly negotiated path until compatible consumers are released and proven.
